searchText: Perhaps a dumb question, but do we need to update any JSON RPC endpoints when 2718+2930 go live? If so, should we aim to put EIPs for these together before Berlin so service providers can know what to expect? They aren't absolutely critical for Berlin. Though, certainly would be nice to have them ready. `eth_sendRawTransaction` expects a legacy transaction. We will probably want something like `eth_sendRawTypedTransaction` which expects a 2718 transaction. Unfortunately, this is one more place where we have to deal with transaction encoding. If we launch Berlin without this in *any* clients, it will be very hard for anyone to actually use 2930. However, clients can individually add endpoints at any time since this isn't a consensus problem. Why shouldn't we allow `sendRawTransaction` to take 2718 txs? I guess we can differentiate from the byte array by the first byte? Does anyone remember off-hand what `eth_sendRawTransaction` expects? Just bytes I believe, that's it For sure, I bet most clients (this is true for besu) just use the same deserialization in the rpc code there so it's almost harder to have it _not_ take 2718 txs Bytes encoded how? https://eth.wiki/json-rpc/API the RLP serialized transaction encoded as hex Sadly, the documentation is lacking... `rlp([nonce, ..., v, r, s])`? I believe so yes Nice. So we should be able to switch internally on the first byte like <@!213672586264051717> suggested. <@!552133098075193354> No new method necessary I think, and depending on client architecture it is possible no additional work needed on that endpoint either. Can we schedule a breakout room next week to further discuss 2718? We need to make sure we're on the same page in terms of encoding. <@!301186049323958275> listed the 3 possibilities: > A. https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/779922457631916064/784269200700473356 is current spec. > B. https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/779922457631916064/784274373883985950 is my proposed alternative spec. > C. https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/779922457631916064/784275462343229540 is lightclient's proposed alternative spec. Happy to schedule a breakout room meeting for EIP-2718 discussion on Monday Dec 07, 2020 at 1500 UTC. If this works, I can send out calendar invite by tomorrow. FWIW we parse the incoming RLP and recover the sender address before sending the tx to the network, and I imagine other infra providers that accept txs do something similar, so we'll need to have those systems EIP-2718 aware before the fork. And I guess we'll need to be aware of each tx type and how to recover the sender for it as well.
